.engramdb/memories/staging-export-bucket-points-at-the-prod-bucket_01a0f910-1e25-7720-9100-c1829851769c.md:15:In staging, `EXPORT_BUCKET` points at the production bucket. Never run scripts/export.py against staging without `--dry-run`.

Yes, but only with `--dry-run`.

A stored project note says that in staging `EXPORT_BUCKET` points at the **production** bucket. A real run against staging could write to prod data.

`scripts/export.py` has a `--dry-run` flag (line 8). It reads `EXPORT_BUCKET` from the environment and defaults to `ledgerline-exports-dev`. I didn't check whether the dry run skips all writes, because the script only prints the bucket and the flag value in the part I grepped. Read the rest of the script before relying on it.

I haven't run anything. The script's argument for the environment is `args.env`. I haven't seen its exact flag or accepted values, so check `--help` first. The command will look something like:

```
python scripts/export.py --env staging --dry-run
```

If you want a real, non-dry test, point `EXPORT_BUCKET` at a dev or scratch bucket first. Don't use the staging value.
